nations.name: Hla'alua
nations.lands: Taoyuan and Namaxia districts, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan

facts.text: In 2014 the Hla'alua were officially recognized as a distinct people, becoming the 15th Indigenous people listed in Taiwan.
The Hla'alua are formed by four communities, Paiciana, Vilanganʉ, Talicia and Hlihlara, in Kaohsiung City.

nations.name: Ainu
nations.lands: Hokkaido and other parts of Japan

facts.text: Upopoy, a national centre for Ainu history and culture in Shiraoi, Hokkaido, opened to the public in July 2020.

source.title: About Upopoy
source.publisher: Upopoy National Ainu Museum and Park

facts.text: A 2019 Japanese law names the Ainu as an Indigenous people of northern Japan, especially Hokkaido, and aims for a society that respects Ainu pride.

source.title: Act on Promoting Measures to Achieve a Society in which the Pride of Ainu People is Respected (Act No. 16 of 2019)
source.publisher: Japanese Law Translation, Ministry of Justice, Japan

nations.name: Sherpa
nations.lands: Solukhumbu and the upper Dudh Koshi and Sun Koshi valleys of northeastern Nepal, from Solu to Helambu, and Kathmandu

facts.text: Sherpa communities use a customary system called nawa to look after crops and forests.

source.title: शेर्पा (Sherpa)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In Nepal's 2021 census, 90.3 percent of Sherpa people reported Sherpa as their own language.

source.title: शेर्पा (Sherpa)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Pangcah
nations.lands: East of the Central Mountain Range in Hualien and Taitung counties, plus the Hengchun Peninsula, Taiwan

facts.text: Their own name, Pangcah, means people and kinsmen. The name Amis came from neighbours in Taitung and was later adopted by scholars.
In some Pangcah communities, each age class takes its name from a key event of its time, so one class name marks the computer era.

nations.name: Karen
nations.lands: Eastern Myanmar, including Karen State, and western and northern Thailand

facts.text: Karen is a name for several related peoples who speak 12 related Karenic languages; about 85 percent of Karen belong to the S'gaw or Pwo branches.
Karen communities have lived in what is now northern Thailand for many centuries.

nations.name: Bodo
nations.lands: Bodoland Territorial Region and other parts of Assam, India

facts.text: Bodo is an associate official language of Assam, and in 2022 the state announced it would become a medium of instruction in Classes XI and XII.

source.title: CM Dr. Sarma attends 61st Annual conference of Bodo Sahitya Sabha (Press Release No. 129/2022)
source.publisher: Directorate of Information and Public Relations, Government of Assam

facts.text: The Bodo Sahitya Sabha, founded on 16 November 1952, has grown into an important body for promoting Bodo language and literature.

source.title: CM Dr. Sarma attends 61st Annual conference of Bodo Sahitya Sabha (Press Release No. 129/2022)
source.publisher: Directorate of Information and Public Relations, Government of Assam

nations.name: Ibaloi
nations.lands: Southern Benguet and the Baguio area in northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: The Ibaloi are one of the three major ethnolinguistic groups of Benguet province, with the Kankanaey and Kalanguya.
Benguet's official provincial fruit is a native blueberry whose Ibaloi name is ayosip.

nations.name: Tripura
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts and other districts of Bangladesh, and the state of Tripura, India

facts.text: Tripura University opened a Department of Kokborok in 2015 and began doctoral research in the language in 2018.
Kokborok, the Tripura language, has been an official language of the Indian state of Tripura since 1979.

nations.name: Magar
nations.lands: Hills of the Rapti and Gandaki river basins in western and central Nepal, and communities across Nepal

facts.text: Magar communities keep customary institutions such as the bheja, and each year they choose a mukhiya as community leader, who settles small disputes.

source.title: मगर (Magar)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Magar as an official language for both Gandaki and Karnali provinces.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

nations.name: Tamu
nations.lands: Tamuwan, the hills between the Trishuli and Kali Gandaki rivers in central Nepal, including Gorkha, Lamjung, Kaski, Syangja, Manang and Mustang

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Gurung, the Tamu language, as an official language of Gandaki Province.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

facts.text: Tamu Kyui, the Tamu language, now has its own Khema script, which Nepal's Language Commission has recognized.

source.title: गुरुङ(तमू) (Gurung, Tamu)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Kalasha
nations.lands: The Kalasha valleys of Bamburet, Birir and Rumbur in the Hindu Kush, Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan

facts.text: Kalasha families use Suri Jagek to choose the right time to sow seeds and care for livestock, and to anticipate natural hazards.
Suri Jagek is practiced at local observatories in three Kalasha valley villages: Bamburet, Birir and Rumbur.

source.title: Pakistan's first independent nomination Suri Jagek inscribed by UNESCO (PR No. 04)
source.publisher: Press Information Department, Government of Pakistan

nations.name: Sakizaya
nations.lands: Hualien Plain, the East Rift Valley and coast, Taiwan

facts.text: Through a cultural revival led by the community itself, the Sakizaya were recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2007.
The Sakizaya population was about 985 in January 2020.

nations.name: Kankanaey
nations.lands: Benguet and Mountain Province in the Cordillera of northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: The Kankanaey are one of the three major ethnolinguistic groups of Benguet province, with the Ibaloi and Kalanguya.
Benguet's official provincial fruit is a native blueberry, known in Kankanaey as gotmo or alumani.

nations.name: Ifugao
nations.lands: Ifugao Province in the Cordillera mountains of northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: Ifugao families still farm and care for their mountain rice terraces, a UNESCO World Heritage living landscape since 1995.

source.title: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras

facts.text: The Hudhud, long narrative chants of the Ifugao sung at rice sowing and harvest, are on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage.

nations.name: Tao
nations.lands: Lanyu (Orchid Island), Taitung County, Taiwan

facts.text: The people call themselves Tao, meaning human, while Yami is the name used officially.
The Tao, who live on Lanyu, also called Orchid Island, numbered 4,684 in January 2020.

nations.name: Mizo
nations.lands: Mizoram, northeast India

facts.text: Mizoram became a full state of India on 20 February 1987; its Legislative Assembly first met on 10 May 1972.
Historically, every Mizo village had its own chief, who was assisted by a council of elders.

nations.name: Chakma
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh, and parts of northeast India

facts.text: Hill Tracts peoples are sometimes called Jumma, after jum, their traditional method of shifting cultivation.
The Chakma make up more than half of the Indigenous population of Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts.

nations.name: Naga
nations.lands: Nagaland, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh in India, and neighbouring Myanmar

facts.text: Nagaland's state portal lists 17 major tribes living in the state, each with its own language and festivals.

source.title: People and Culture
source.publisher: Nagaland State Portal, Government of Nagaland

facts.text: Each December the Government of Nagaland hosts the Hornbill Festival near Kohima, where all the state's tribes share their cultures.

nations.name: Newa
nations.lands: Swanigah, the Kathmandu Valley (Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur), and towns across Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Nepal Bhasa, alongside Tamang, as an official language of Bagmati Province.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

facts.text: Nepal Bhasa, the Newa language, has its own scripts, Ranjana and Prachalit, along with its own grammar, dictionaries and literature.

source.title: नेवार (Newar)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Garo
nations.lands: Garo Hills of Meghalaya, India, and north-central Bangladesh

facts.text: The Garo Hills Autonomous District Council, set up in 1952 under India's Sixth Schedule, is based in Tura and covers five districts.
The Meghalaya government lists Garo among the state's languages, alongside Khasi, Pnar and English.

nations.name: Orang Asli
nations.lands: Peninsular Malaysia

facts.text: Orang Asli, a Malay collective term meaning original or first peoples, covers 18 officially listed groups of Peninsular Malaysia.
Some Temuan, Jakun and Semai families now run their own rubber, oil palm or cocoa farms.

nations.name: Atayal
nations.lands: Mountain areas of northern and central Taiwan, across New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu, Miaoli, Taichung, Nantou and Yilan

facts.text: In the Atayal language, the word Atayal means people, real people, or kinspeople.
The Atayal live across the mountains of northern and central Taiwan, the widest spread of any Indigenous people on the island.

nations.name: Iban
nations.lands: Sarawak, Malaysia, with communities in West Kalimantan, Indonesia, and Brunei

facts.text: Between 1948 and 1963 the Iban language served as the common language between Sarawak's communities.

source.title: Indigenous peoples and ethnic minorities in Sarawak

facts.text: In 2011 the Tun Jugah Foundation published Bup Sereba Reti Jaku Iban, described as the first monolingual Iban dictionary.

nations.name: Mru
nations.lands: Bandarban district in the Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh, and nearby areas of Myanmar

facts.text: The Mru alphabet, invented in the 1980s and unrelated to any other script, is encoded in the Unicode Standard with its own digits.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: School textbooks up to class three have been published in the Mru language and alphabet.

nations.name: Kavalan
nations.lands: Yilan and the Hualien and Taitung coasts, Taiwan

facts.text: After a name rectification movement, the Kavalan were officially recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2002.
The Kavalan population was about 1,492 in January 2020.

nations.name: Kadazandusun
nations.lands: Sabah, Malaysia

facts.text: The Kadazan Dusun Cultural Association, founded in 1966, represents 48 Indigenous ethnic communities of Sabah.
KDCA works on preserving, standardizing and developing the Kadazandusun language with its many dialects.

nations.name: Rapa Nui
nations.lands: Rapa Nui (Easter Island), in the south-eastern Pacific, Chile

facts.text: Tapati Rapa Nui, the island's main cultural festival, filled two weeks of February 2026 with ancestral competitions, arts and celebrations of Rapa Nui identity, language and traditions.

source.title: Ministra de las Culturas participa en inauguración de la Tapati Rapanui y desarrolla agenda de trabajo en la isla
source.publisher: Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio (Chile)

facts.text: In 2017, 642 votes were cast in a formal consultation with the Rapa Nui people on a marine protected area for their island, and yes won all three questions.

source.title: Informe del Proceso de Consulta al pueblo Rapa Nui sobre creación, administración y regulación de usos de un Área Marina Costera Protegida de Múltiples Usos para Rapa Nui
source.publisher: Ministerio del Medio Ambiente, Gobierno de Chile

nations.name: Aṉangu
nations.lands: Central Australia, including Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa in the Northern Territory and the APY Lands of South Australia

facts.text: The park's board of management has 12 people, including eight Aboriginal members nominated by Traditional Owners.

source.title: Joint management | Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park | Parks Australia

facts.text: Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park was handed back to its Aṉangu Traditional Owners in 1985 and is jointly managed today.

source.title: Joint management | Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park | Parks Australia

nations.name: Cook Islands Māori
nations.lands: the Cook Islands, including Rarotonga and the Southern and Northern Group islands

facts.text: Te Maeva Nui, held every early August, marks Cook Islands self-governance on 4 August and gathers communities from every island for song, dance, drumming and chant.
A 2003 law declared Cook Islands Māori an official language of the Cook Islands, alongside English, and set up a Māori language commission.

source.title: Te Reo Maori Act 2003 (Cook Islands)
source.publisher: Université Laval, CEFAN: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde

nations.name: Moriori
nations.lands: Rēkohu and Rangihaute (the Chatham and Pitt Islands), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Moriori are the Indigenous people of Rēkohu and Rangihaute, the Chatham Islands, and are represented by the Hokotehi Moriori Trust.
The Hokotehi Moriori Trust takes part in key parts of the Rēkohu economy, such as fishing, farming and tourism.

nations.name: Gadigal
nations.lands: The southern side of Sydney Harbour (Port Jackson), from South Head to around Petersham, in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia

facts.text: Descendants of the Eora still live in Sydney today and proudly use the name Eora.
The City of Sydney formally acknowledges the Gadigal of the Eora Nation as the traditional custodians of the place now called Sydney.

nations.name: Larrakia
nations.lands: The Darwin region, from Cox Peninsula in the west to Gunn Point in the north, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Larrakia Nation Aboriginal Corporation, set up in 1997, runs about 40 programs in Darwin, including the Larrakia Land and Sea Rangers.
Larrakia are the traditional owners of the Darwin region, with country reaching from Cox Peninsula in the west up to Gunn Point in the north.

nations.name: Marshallese
nations.lands: the atolls and islands of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, including Majuro

facts.text: Waan Aelõñ in Majel, Canoes of the Marshall Islands, is a Majuro program that trains young Marshallese women and men in skills for a sustainable future.

source.title: Canoes of the Marshall Islands, Waan Aelõñ in Majel

facts.text: A Marshallese stick chart maps how ocean swells bend around islands, with cowrie shells for the islands, and is studied before a voyage rather than used at sea.

source.title: Stick Navigation Chart
source.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History

nations.name: Kaurna
nations.lands: The Adelaide Plains of South Australia, from around Crystal Brook in the north, bounded by the Mount Lofty Ranges to the east, Australia

facts.text: In March 2018 Kaurna people were recognised as native title holders around Adelaide, the first positive native title determination over a capital city area.

source.title: Native Title Recognition For Kaurna People Over Adelaide Area

facts.text: Requests for Kaurna names and translations all go through Kaurna Warra Karrpanthi, an Aboriginal corporation.

source.title: Aboriginal people of South Australia: Kaurna

nations.name: Torres Strait Islanders
nations.lands: the islands of the Torres Strait between Cape York and Papua New Guinea, in Queensland, Australia, and the Northern Peninsula Area

facts.text: The Torres Strait Regional Authority, an Australian Government body set up on 1 July 1994, counts recognising and maintaining Torres Strait Islander Ailan Kastom among its functions.
Kala Lagaw Ya is the traditional language of the western and central Torres Strait islands, and Meriam Mir is the language of the eastern islands.

nations.name: Noongar
nations.lands: The south-west of Western Australia, including the Perth region, Australia

facts.text: Western Australia's settlement recognises the Noongar people as the traditional owners of the South-West, with about A$1.3 billion in land and other benefits.

source.title: All six South West Native Title Settlement Agreements registered

facts.text: The South West Native Title Settlement covers about 200,000 square kilometres and affects an estimated 40,000 Noongar people.

source.title: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council
source.publisher: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council

nations.name: Yolŋu
nations.lands: North-east Arnhem Land, including the Gove Peninsula, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Yolŋu elders founded Dhimurru Aboriginal Corporation to manage their land on the Gove Peninsula and the visitors who come to it.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

facts.text: The name Dhimurru means east wind, the wind that carries the monsoon rains and brings new life to the land.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

nations.name: Waikato-Tainui
nations.lands: The Waikato region of the North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui describes itself as a growing tribe of over 90,000 people, voyagers and pioneers like their ancestors.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui celebrate their identity as people of the Tainui waka and as protectors of the Kiingitanga movement.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

nations.name: Niueans
nations.lands: the island of Niue in the South Pacific, with villages such as Alofi, Mutalau and Toi

facts.text: Fale Tāoga Niue, home of the Niue National Museum, opened on 19 October 2018, the anniversary of the Niue Constitution Celebrations.
Niue's Vagahau Niue Act 2012 recognises Vagahau Niue as the official language of Niue and created the Niue Language Commission to protect it.

source.title: Vagahau Niue Act 2012
source.publisher: Université Laval, CEFAN: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde

nations.name: Samoans
nations.lands: the Independent State of Samoa, on Upolu, Savai'i and nearby islands

facts.text: Women and master weavers have formed fine mat committees in their villages, and more young women, and some men, now weave the 'ie Samoa.

source.title: 'Ie Samoa, fine mat and its cultural value

facts.text: Samoa's 2021 census counted 16,082 people aged 21 and over who hold a matai, or chiefly, title, including 1,444 women.

source.title: Samoa Population and Housing Census 2021 Fact Sheet (Final Results, October 2022)

nations.name: Chuukese
nations.lands: Chuuk State in the Federated States of Micronesia, on the high islands of Chuuk Lagoon such as Weno, Tonoas, Uman and Fefan, and outlying atolls

facts.text: Chuuk's state constitution says existing Chuukese custom and tradition shall be respected, and lets traditional leaders hold formal roles in government.

source.title: Chuuk State Constitution, Article IV
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Chuuk's constitution recognizes traditional rights over all reefs, tidelands and other submerged lands, including the water above them.

source.title: Chuuk State Constitution, Article IV
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Palauans
nations.lands: the Republic of Palau in the western Pacific, with 16 states on Babeldaob, Koror and other islands

facts.text: Palauans still use the Rock Islands Southern Lagoon, a World Heritage site since 2012, for cultural purposes under a traditional governance system.
Palau's Council of Chiefs, made up of the highest traditional chiefs from each state, advises the President on traditional laws and customs.

nations.name: Gunantuna
nations.lands: the Gazelle Peninsula of New Britain Island, East New Britain Province, Papua New Guinea

facts.text: Diwarra pays for everyday things such as store goods and school fees, and sharing it out expresses ties between clans and individuals.

source.title: Gunantuna (Tolai people)
source.publisher: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art

facts.text: In 2016 a Queensland gallery commissioned A Bit na Ta, a collaborative work made with the wider Tolai community whose music carries the rhythms of Tolai life from 1875 to 1975.

source.title: Art from Papua New Guinea Celebrated in Major QAG Exhibition
source.publisher: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art

nations.name: Whanganui Iwi
nations.lands: The Whanganui River, from the mountains to the sea, North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui, the iwi river trust, was established in August 2014 with the signing of Ruruku Whakatupua.

source.title: Home | Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui

facts.text: Since 2017, New Zealand law has recognised the Whanganui River, Te Awa Tupua, as a legal person, with a guardian office that acts as its human face.

source.title: The Whanganui River (Te Awa Tupua)
source.publisher: OsloMet (Oslo Metropolitan University), River Rights project

nations.name: Ngāi Tahu
nations.lands: Te Waipounamu (the South Island), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: There are 18 Papatipu Rūnanga, local Ngāi Tahu councils, spread throughout Te Waipounamu, the South Island.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

facts.text: Ngāi Tahu means people of Tahu, and whakapapa, the ancestral link, binds all Ngāi Tahu whānau.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

nations.name: Nauruans
nations.lands: the island of Nauru, officially styled Naoero, in the central Pacific

facts.text: Nauru's government now presents the country as the Republic of Naoero on its official website.

source.title: The Government of the Republic of Naoero
source.publisher: Government of the Republic of Nauru

facts.text: In Nauru's 2021 census, 69 percent of residents aged 5 and over spoke only Nauruan at home, and another 25.3 percent spoke it with another language.

source.title: Nauru 2021 Population and Housing Census: Analytical Report

nations.name: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei
nations.lands: Central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei's shared affairs are looked after by their Trust and two subsidiaries: Whai Māia, the social arm, and Whai Rawa, the commercial arm.
Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei are the tangata whenua, the people of the land, of Te Kahu Tōpuni o Tuperiri in central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland).

nations.name: Refaluwasch
nations.lands: Saipan and other islands of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, a United States commonwealth in the western Pacific

facts.text: In December 2020 the Matawal Wóól Display Hall opened with photos and crafts made by students of the Tepengi Kkosch Refaluwasch culture program.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2021 Citizen Centric Report

facts.text: The Carolinian Affairs Office, created by the CNMI Constitution, advises the governor and works to protect and preserve the culture and traditions of Indigenous Carolinians.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2020 Citizen Centric Report

nations.name: Pohnpeians
nations.lands: Pohnpei State in the Federated States of Micronesia, on Pohnpei island and its outlying atolls

facts.text: Nan Madol, a World Heritage site since 2016, is traditionally owned and managed under the Nahnmwarki system, a chiefly institution that continues in Pohnpei today.

source.title: Nan Madol: Ceremonial Centre of Eastern Micronesia

facts.text: Pohnpei State's constitution protects the customs and traditions of Pohnpei's traditional kingdoms alongside its elected government.

source.title: Pohnpei
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Delaware Nation
nations.lands: Anadarko, Oklahoma, United States; Lenape homelands on the Eastern Seaboard

facts.text: Delaware Nation is a federally recognized tribe based in Anadarko, Oklahoma.
In December 2022 Delaware Nation re-established its Tribal Historic Preservation Office to identify and protect cultural resources in Lenape homelands.

source.title: Delaware Nation Re-Established THPO Status with the National Park Services and US Department of Interior

nations.name: Wampanoag Tribe of Gay Head (Aquinnah)
nations.lands: Aquinnah, on the western end of Martha's Vineyard (Noepe), Massachusetts, United States

facts.text: The Aquinnah Wampanoag care for 477 acres of their ancestral lands on Martha's Vineyard.
In 1998 the town of Gay Head returned to its former Wampanoag name, Aquinnah.

nations.name: Tuscarora Nation
nations.lands: Tuscarora Nation territory near Lewiston, western New York, United States; earlier homelands in what is now North Carolina

facts.text: The Tuscarora Language Program works with one clear mission: to revive a community of Tuscarora speakers.
The Tuscarora Environment Program works as part of the Haudenosaunee Environmental Task Force, established in 1992 by the Grand Council.

nations.name: Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe
nations.lands: Mashpee on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, United States; Wampanoag homelands across present-day Massachusetts and eastern Rhode Island

facts.text: The Mashpee Wampanoag were re-acknowledged as a federally recognized tribe in 2007.

source.title: Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe | People of the First Light

facts.text: Children at Mukayuhsak Weekuw, the Mashpee Wampanoag language nest, could be the first in centuries to grow up proficient in Wôpanâak.

nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the Chickahominy River area and Chickahominy Ridge in Virginia, as described in the Tribe's history

facts.text: The Chickahominy Indian Tribe's history describes permanent villages along the Virginia river that still bears its name.
The Tribe dates the establishment of Samaria Indian Baptist Church, a community institution, to 1901.

nations.name: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma
nations.lands: Tahlequah, Oklahoma, United States

facts.text: The UKB Tribal Council is made up of four officers and nine district representatives, governing from Tahlequah, Oklahoma.

source.title: United Keetoowah Band | Home | Tahlequah, OK
source.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma

facts.text: The United Keetoowah Band numbers more than 14,000 tribal members today.

source.title: About Us | United Keetoowah Band | Tahlequah
source.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma

pronounce.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma, on its own site

nations.name: Monacan Indian Nation
nations.lands: Bear Mountain in Amherst County, Virginia; the Nation describes ancestral homelands extending through Virginia and parts of West Virginia and North Carolina

facts.text: The Nation says its Priority Climate Action Plan includes a greenhouse gas inventory to guide conservation and emissions-reduction work.
The Nation describes its citizens as descendants of Virginia and North Carolina Eastern Siouan cultural and linguistic groups.

nations.name: Nansemond Indian Nation
nations.lands: the Nansemond River area of southeastern Virginia; the Nation describes traditional settlements extending into northeastern North Carolina

facts.text: The Nation's published Environmental Program describes oyster restoration, invasive plant removal and native plant restoration.
The Nation's history dates formal organization with elected officers to 1984.

nations.name: Muscogee Nation
nations.lands: Okmulgee and the Muscogee reservation in eastern Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Georgia and Alabama

facts.text: Seated in Okmulgee, Oklahoma, the Muscogee (Creek) Nation is self-governed and organized by its Constitution into three branches of government.
The Mvskoke Language Program offers classes and learning resources so Mvskoke people can keep their language, culture and sovereignty strong.

nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe - Eastern Division
nations.lands: New Kent County, Virginia; the Tribe describes roots in Virginia before English colonization

facts.text: In its food-sovereignty account, CIT-ED says a 2022 EPA grant supported a community compost and gardening program.
The Tribe's timeline records a certificate of incorporation for the Chickahominy Indians Eastern Division in 1925.

nations.name: Narragansett Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Rhode Island, United States

facts.text: The Narragansett Indian Tribe received federal recognition and acknowledgement on April 11, 1983.
A land claim brought by the Tribe ended in a 1978 out-of-court settlement of about 1,800 acres.

nations.name: Passamaquoddy (Peskotomuhkati)
nations.lands: Sipayik (Pleasant Point) and Motahkomikuk (Indian Township) in Maine, United States, and a community in New Brunswick, Canada

facts.text: Over 3,000 Passamaquoddy citizens belong to three self-governing communities, two in Maine and one in New Brunswick, linked by political, cultural and kinship ties.
The Maliseet-Passamaquoddy Dictionary has more than 19,000 entries, and many older tribal members still speak the language fluently.

nations.name: MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians
nations.lands: Mobile and Washington Counties in southwestern Alabama, near the Mobile and Tombigbee Rivers

facts.text: The Tribe's introduction places its communities in Mobile and Washington Counties in southwestern Alabama.
Its history dates an effort to obtain federal aid for Alabama Choctaw schools to 1934.

source.title: Social Barriers - MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians

nations.name: Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians
nations.lands: Choctaw communities in east-central Mississippi, United States

facts.text: In 1945 the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians ratified a Constitution that authorized the Tribe's separation from the state of Mississippi.

source.title: About Us - Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians

facts.text: The Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians has more than 11,000 tribal members.

nations.name: Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Durant and a reservation of eight whole and five partial counties in southeastern Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Mississippi

facts.text: Chahta Anumpa Aiikhvna, the School of Choctaw Language, offers classes for every skill level plus a Speak Choctaw app.
The Choctaw Nation reservation covers 10,864 square miles in southeastern Oklahoma, taking in eight whole counties and parts of five more.

nations.name: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Southampton County, Virginia, United States

facts.text: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe is based in Southampton County, Virginia.
The Tribe's language page publishes a vocabulary drawn from materials dating to March 4, 1820.

nations.lands: East Texas; the Tribe describes its reservation in the Big Thicket

facts.text: The Tribe's government page states that its elected Tribal Council members serve three-year terms.
The Tribe describes an elected Tribal Council advised by its Chiefs. The profile concerns this Texas Tribal government, not every Alabama or Coushatta community.

nations.name: Shinnecock Indian Nation
nations.lands: In and around the Town of Southampton on the eastern end of Long Island, New York, United States

facts.text: On October 1, 2010, the Shinnecock Indian Nation was formally recognized by the United States as the 565th federally recognized tribe.
The Shinnecock Indian Nation has over 1,589 enrolled tribal members.

nations.name: Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia
nations.lands: southeastern Virginia along the Nottoway River; the Tribe's Community House & Interpretive Center is in Capron

facts.text: The Tribe's history describes the Nottoway as Iroquoian speakers of southeastern Virginia.

source.title: Tribal History - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

source.title: Community House & Interpretive Center - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

nations.name: Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina
nations.lands: Along the Lumbee River in Robeson, Hoke, Cumberland and Scotland counties, North Carolina, United States, centered on Pembroke

facts.text: The Lumbee Tribe became fully federally recognized by the United States on December 18, 2025.
The Lumbee Tribe describes its people, the People of the Dark Water, as entrepreneurial and strongly focused on education.

nations.name: Oneida Indian Nation
nations.lands: Central New York, United States

facts.text: Oneida Indian Nation Members learn Onyota’a:ká:, the Oneida language, through intensive courses, a preschool curriculum, e-books, smartphone apps and an Oneida language keyboard.
During the American Revolution, Oneidas fought alongside the colonists and carried corn to feed General Washington's starving soldiers; the Nation honors them as America's first allies.

nations.name: Imazighen
nations.lands: North Africa (Tamazgha): Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt's Siwa oasis, with communities across the Sahel and in the diaspora

facts.text: After decades of campaigning, Tamazight was recognized as a national and official language in Algeria's Constitution in 2016.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Algeria
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Morocco
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Griqua
nations.lands: the Western Cape, Eastern Cape, Northern Cape, Free State and KwaZulu-Natal provinces of South Africa

facts.text: Griqua communities live today in the Western Cape, Eastern Cape, Northern Cape, Free State and KwaZulu-Natal.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Early Griqua communities governed themselves through leaders called kaptyns, with magistrates drawn from leading families.

nations.name: Siwans
nations.lands: the oases of Siwa and El-Gara in Egypt's Western Desert, near the border with Libya

facts.text: A sense of Berber belonging has revived in Siwa this century; a letter of the Tifinagh alphabet, the Amazigh symbol, now names a bazaar below old Shali.

source.title: Siwa, the Berber oasis where cultures cross (An Atlas of Contemporary Egypt, 2023)

facts.text: Ten Siwan tribes speak Siwi, an eastern Amazigh (Berber) language, in the oases of Siwa and El-Gara.

source.title: Siwa, the Berber oasis where cultures cross (An Atlas of Contemporary Egypt, 2023)

nations.name: Khwe
nations.lands: north-eastern Namibia, north-western Botswana and southern Angola, and Platfontein near Kimberley in South Africa

facts.text: In South Africa, Khwe and !Xun communities live mainly at Platfontein, near Kimberley.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Khwe people in Namibia have their own Traditional Authority. As of 2025 the government had not recognized it, which Khwe say makes land and development issues harder to resolve.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Namibia
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Ogiek
nations.lands: highland forests of Kenya, especially the Mau Forest

facts.text: In December 2025 the African Court issued its first ever compliance decision, in the Ogiek case, finding that Kenya had not yet carried out its judgments.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Kenya
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2017 the African Court ruled for the Ogiek, its first ruling for an Indigenous people, and recognized Indigenous peoples as guardians of local ecosystems.

nations.name: Datooga
nations.lands: northern Tanzania, including the highlands near Mount Hanang in Manyara Region and the Lake Eyasi area

facts.text: Datooga and Hadza communities own more than 110,000 hectares of dryland forest protected through the Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape project.
With help from the NGO Ujamaa Community Resource Team, Barabaig communities in northern Tanzania gained grazing land held under collective title.

nations.name: Hai//om
nations.lands: north-central Namibia, in and around Etosha National Park and on resettlement farms in Kunene, Oshikoto and Oshana regions

facts.text: In July 2026 Namibia's Vice President opened a high-level meeting in Outjo with the Hai//om Traditional Authority on a development plan for Hai//om communities.

source.title: Government Reaffirms Commitment to Hai-//om Community Development, Vice President Lucia Witbooi (speech)

facts.text: Many Hai//om communities lived on lands that are now Etosha National Park and the surrounding regions, according to the Hai//om Community San Council.

source.title: Challenges Faced by the Hai//om San Marginalized Communities in Namibia: Challenges and Solutions
source.publisher: Cultural Survival (by the Hai//om Community San Council)

nations.name: Wodaabe
nations.lands: the Sahel of Niger, with communities in Chad, northern Cameroon and north-east Nigeria

facts.text: In 2008 thousands of Wodaabe herders attended the fourth General Assembly of the Woodaabe Pastoralists of Niger.

source.title: Oromo pastoralists visit Woodaabe General Assembly in Niger

facts.text: Cattle herding is the main livelihood of the Wodaabe, who move with the seasons across the Sahel.

nations.name: Konso
nations.lands: the Konso highlands of south-western Ethiopia

facts.text: The Konso built the dry-stone terraces of their highlands and still farm them; UNESCO lists the Konso Cultural Landscape as World Heritage.
The Konso raise stone steles to mark the handing of responsibility from the older generation to the younger, a living tradition.

nations.name: Kel Tamasheq
nations.lands: the Sahara and Sahel: northern Mali and Niger, southern Algeria and Libya, and northern Burkina Faso

facts.text: In Libya, the Fezzan region, including Ubari and Ghat, is traditional Kel Tamasheq territory, linked to communities across the borders in Niger and Algeria.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Libya
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In Niger, Kel Tamasheq (Tuareg) herders raise camels and goats in Agadez, Tahoua and Tillabéry. Estimates for 2009 put them at about 1.2 million, 8.3% of the population.

source.title: Indigenous World 2020: Niger
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Endorois
nations.lands: around Lake Bogoria in Baringo County, and in Nakuru and Laikipia counties, in Kenya's Rift Valley

facts.text: The Endorois Welfare Council, founded in 1995 by senior members of the community, works for justice and sustainable development for the Endorois.

source.title: Endorois Welfare Council - Endorois Welfare Council for marginalized communities

facts.text: In 2010 the African Union approved an African Commission ruling in the Endorois case, the first in Africa to recognize Indigenous peoples' rights to land they traditionally owned.

source.title: Landmark decision rules Kenya’s removal of indigenous people from ancestral land illegal

nations.name: Yiaku
nations.lands: Mukogodo Forest in Laikipia County, Kenya

facts.text: Yiaku women and elders now lead language teaching and forest care, and growing youth involvement is strengthening the community.

source.title: Reviving Indigenous forest stewardship
source.publisher: International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED)

facts.text: Since 2003 the Yiaku Laikipiak Trust has worked to protect Mukogodo Forest and keep Yiaku culture alive.

source.title: Reviving Indigenous forest stewardship
source.publisher: International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED)

nations.name: Anywaa
nations.lands: Gambella in western Ethiopia, along the Akobo, Alwaro, Openo (Baro) and Gilo rivers, and neighbouring South Sudan

facts.text: Anywaa activists helped found EMIPRO in 2022, the first legally registered Indigenous-led rights organization in Ethiopia.

source.title: “We Belong to This Land:” The Anywaa Peoples’ Fight for Survival, Dignity, and Recognition in Ethiopia

facts.text: The Anywaa are river farmers and fishers whose lives follow the Akobo, Alwaro, Openo (Baro) and Gilo rivers of Gambella.

source.title: “We Belong to This Land:” The Anywaa Peoples’ Fight for Survival, Dignity, and Recognition in Ethiopia

nations.name: Toubou
nations.lands: the Tibesti plateau of northern Chad, southern Libya along the Chad border, and northern Niger

facts.text: Toubou herders practise mobile pastoralism across a wide area stretching from northern Niger to Sudan.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Libya chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: About 50,000 Toubou live in Libya along the border with Chad; the people's origins lie in the Tibesti plateau.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Libya chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Rifians
nations.lands: the Rif of northern and north-eastern Morocco, including Al Hoceima province

facts.text: In Morocco's 2024 census, 53.6% of people in Al Hoceima province said they use Tarifit, the language of the Irifiyen.

source.title: RGPH 2024: Caractéristiques démographiques et socioéconomiques de la population, Région Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceima

facts.text: Nationwide, 3.2% of Morocco's population reported Tarifit among the local languages they use, in the 2024 census.

source.title: RGPH 2024: Caractéristiques démographiques et socioéconomiques de la population, Région Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceima

nations.name: Baka
nations.lands: forests of eastern and southern Cameroon, northern Gabon, and neighbouring parts of the Republic of the Congo and Central African Republic

facts.text: In Gabon, the Baka are one of nine Indigenous forest peoples, alongside the Babongo, Bakoya and others, each with its own language and culture.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Gabon chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2025 a Batouri workshop run by the association ASBABUK and Cameroon's forestry ministry focused on fully recognizing Baka as rightful partners in managing forest resources.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Cameroon
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Sengwer
nations.lands: Cherangany Hills and Embobut Forest in Kenya's western highlands

facts.text: Sengwer society is organized around clans, each with its own roles, and elders guide decisions and teach younger generations.
Sengwer knowledge includes sustainable ways of hunting, gathering, beekeeping and caring for forest resources, which helps conserve biodiversity.

nations.name: Kabyles
nations.lands: Kabylia in north-eastern Algeria, with a large community in France

facts.text: Taqbaylit, the Kabyle language, is one of three Amazigh languages taught from bachelor's level to doctorate at Inalco in Paris.

source.title: Kabyle (Berber)
source.publisher: Inalco (Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales)

facts.text: Kabyles make up around half of Algeria's Amazigh population, centred on Kabylia in the north-east.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Algeria chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Mozabite
nations.lands: the M'Zab valley around Ghardaïa in the Algerian Sahara

facts.text: UNESCO credits the M'Zab with an ingenious system for capturing and sharing water which, with its palm groves, makes life work in a semi-desert.
The M'Zab valley habitat, built in the tenth century by the Ibadites around five ksour (fortified towns), survives intact and is UNESCO World Heritage.

nations.name: BaAka
nations.lands: forests between the Oubangui and Sangha rivers, in south-western Central African Republic and northern Republic of the Congo

facts.text: Dzanga-Sangha Protected Areas credits BaAka knowledge of the forest as central to its research, conservation and tourism work.
The Central African Republic, home to many BaAka communities, ratified ILO Convention 169 on Indigenous peoples in 2010, the first African state to do so.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2021: Central African Republic
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
nations.lands: Northern Cheyenne Reservation, southeastern Montana, United States; headquarters in Lame Deer

source.title: Northern Cheyenne Tribe

nations.lands: Southwest Oklahoma, United States; headquarters north of Lawton

facts.text: The Comanche Nation's main governing body is its Tribal Council, made up of every enrolled member over age 18.
The Comanche Nation language program works to revitalize and reclaim the Comanche language, including through online learning.

pronounce.text: Nʉmʉnʉʉ, the Comanche name for the people: NUH-MUH-NUH

source.title: Crow Nation

nations.name: Spirit Lake Nation

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.lands: Apache and Fletcher, Oklahoma; reservation land in New Mexico, United States

facts.text: The Fort Sill Apache Tribe comprises descendants of Chiricahua and Warm Springs Apaches displaced from the Southwest and northern Mexico.
The General Council, made up of adult tribal members, elects the Business Committee and approves the tribal operations budget.

nations.name: Oneida Nation
also: Oneida Tribe of Indians of Wisconsin
nations.lands: Oneida Reservation, Brown and Outagamie counties, northeast Wisconsin, United States

source.title: Oneida Nation | Department of Public Instruction

nations.name: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Oklahoma; the Tribe publishes its offices in Ponca City

source.title: Historic Preservation

nations.name: Citizen Potawatomi Nation
nations.lands: Headquartered in Shawnee, Oklahoma, United States, with citizens around the world

facts.text: In July 2026 the Citizen Potawatomi Nation signed the articles of confederation for the Potawatomi Confederacy.
The Citizen Potawatomi Nation Constitution dates from 1938 and was amended in 1985 and again in 2007.

nations.name: Kaw Nation
nations.lands: Oklahoma, with historical homelands in Kansas and the Great Plains

facts.text: The Nation's history distinguishes a Tribal Council from a General Council composed of enrolled adult citizens.
The Nation's language page lists online learning and a basic Kanza course. Listed materials remain under the publisher's access and use conditions.

nations.name: Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate
nations.lands: Lake Traverse Reservation, northeastern South Dakota and southeastern North Dakota, United States

facts.text: The Lake Traverse Reservation reaches across seven counties, five in South Dakota and two in North Dakota.
The Oyate counts more than 14,000 tribal members, living across the United States and serving abroad in the Armed Forces.

nations.name: Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes
nations.lands: Western Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Concho

facts.text: The Cheyenne and Arapaho Language Program offers classes in tribal communities and online for tribal members.

source.title: Language and Culture | Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes

source.title: Language and Culture | Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes

nations.name: Meskwaki Nation
also: Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa
nations.lands: Meskwaki Settlement near Tama, Iowa, United States

source.title: History | Meskwaki | Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi
source.publisher: Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa

facts.text: The Meskwaki language is close to the Sauk and Kickapoo dialects, and the people are working hard to keep it strong.

source.publisher: Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa

nations.name: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community
nations.lands: Scott County, Minnesota, United States

facts.text: Following the Dakota tradition of helping others, the SMSC gives millions of dollars each year to other tribes, organizations and local governments.

source.title: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community in Scott County, MN

facts.text: The community says plainly that it is still here, living traditional Dakota lifeways that will pass on to future generations.

source.title: Our History - Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community in Scott County, MN

nations.name: Caddo Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Oklahoma, with offices in Binger; the Nation describes ancestral homelands in present-day Oklahoma, Louisiana, Arkansas and Texas

facts.text: The Nation's Historic Preservation Department describes work in repatriation and consultation, and publishes separate procedures for Section 106 and NAGPRA requests.
The Nation dates the beginning of its current language program to August 1, 2022. This institutional milestone does not date the start of Caddo language preservation.

nations.name: Oglala Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Pine Ridge Reservation, southwestern South Dakota, United States

facts.text: The Pine Ridge Reservation, home of the Oglala Sioux Tribe, covers about 2.1 million acres across Oglala Lakota, Jackson and Bennett counties in South Dakota.

source.title: Pine Ridge Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs
